sentences.text: In order to lodge a proper complaint, mere mention of the Sections and the language of those sections is not be all and end of the matter.

What is required to be brought to the notice of the Court is the particulars of the offence committed by each and every accused and the role played by each and every accused in committing of that offence.
when we see the complaint, the compliant is sadly vague.
it does not show as to which accused has committed what offence and what is the exact role played by these appellants in the commission of offence.
there could be said something against Rajesh, as the allegations are made against him more precisely but he is no more and has already expired.

Under such circumstances, it would be an abuse of a process of law to allow the prosecution to continue against the aged parents of Rajesh, the present appellant herein on the basis of vague to continue against the aged parents of Rajesh, the present appellants herein on the basis of vague and general complaint which is silent about the precise acts of the appellants"
and the complaint was quashed."
"6. The High Court has merely mentioned that the allegation in the complaint are of retaining jewellery articles in possession of the husband the petitioners.
Now, if the articles were it he possession of the husband, there is no question of the present appellants being in possession of the jewellerty.

This is apart from the fact that it has already been expressed by us that there is no mention of the date on which the said ornaments, if any, were entrusted to the appellants or even the date when they were demanded back and were refused to be given back by the appellants or any one of them.
In so far as the offence under Section 498A IPC is concerned, we do not find any material or allegation worth the name against the present appellants.
All the allegations appear to be against the Rajesh."

The Lordship of Supreme Court in case ' Union of India vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal', (1979) 3 SCC 4, this Court after adverting to the conditions enumerated in Section 227 of the Code and other decisions of this Court, enunciated the following principles:-
"(1) That the Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under Section 227 of the Code has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.

entities.text: Union of India vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal', (1979) 3 SCC 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly eXplained the Court will be fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.
(3) The test to determine a prima facie case would naturally depend upon the facts of each case and it is difficult to lay down a rule of universal application.

By and large however if two views are equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence produced before him while giving rise to some suspicion but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused.

(4) That in eXercising his jurisdiction under Section 227 of the Code the Judge which under the present Code is a senior and eXperienced court cannot act merely as a Post Office or a mouthpiece of the prosecution, but has to consider the broad probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court,
any basic infirmities appearing in the case and so on.
This however does not mean that the Judge should make a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial."

18. Since, their Lordship of Lordship of Supreme Court in case 'Dilawar Balu Kurane vs. State of Maharashtra (Appeal. (Crl.) 8 of 2002" was pleased to hold that:
"When two views are possible, then the view in favour of the accused has to be adopted by the court".

The respondent no.3/complainant has levelled allegations against the petitioner (in her statement recorded u/s. 164 of CrPC on dated 13.09.2017 that this petitioner had asked that the complainant should not give birth to a female child (when the complainant was pregnant) and stated that she had brought a scooty not motorcycle.

Such allegations do not fall within the ambits of either explanation 'a' or 'b' appended to the provision of Sec. 498- A of IPC.
23.

In case of "Mohan Singh and Anr. vs. State of M.P. (1999) 1 Supreme Court Reports 276", it was held that:
"the courts have been removing chaff from the grain.

entities.text: Mohan Singh and Anr. vs. State of M.P. (1999) 1 Supreme Court Reports 276
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has to disperse the suspicious cloud and dust out the smear of dust as all these things clog the very truth.
So long chaff, cloud and dust remains, the criminals are clothed with this protective layer to receive the benefit of doubt.
So it is a solemn duty of the courts, not to merely conclude and leave the case the moment suspicions are created.
It is onerous duty of the court, within permissible limit to find out the truth.
It means, on the one hand no innocent man should be punished but on the other hand to see no person committing an offence should go scott free.
If in spite of such effort suspicion is not dissolved, it remains writ at large, benefit of doubt has to be credited to the accused."

It is also clear that when two views are possible then the view goes in favour of the accused has to be adopted.

Since, in the case in hand, the marriage between the respondent no. 3 / complainant and son of the petitioner/accused was solemnized on dated 10.02.2003 and complaint (on the basis of which the FIR has been registered) was filed by the respondent no. 3 / complainant on dated 08.10.2012 and FIR has been registered on dated 08.11.2014 and the perusal of the complaint dated 08.10.2012 and FIR reveal that there was no allegation against the petitioner.

It is worthwhile to mention here that on dated 13.09.2017, the statement of the respondent no. 3 / complainant was recorded u/s.
164 of CrPC by the Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate, wherein, she had levelled the allegation against the petitioner and in view of delay in recording of such statement of the respondent no. 3 / complainant,
the possibility of introduction of an afterthought and colourful version cannot be ruled out.
No doubt that at the time of framing of charge, only prima facie case is required to be seen.

But, in the considered opinion of this court, the Ld. Trial Court could see all such aspect of the case, as,
discussed herein above at the time of framing of the charge u/s. 498-A/34 of IPC against the petitioner/accused.
But, the Ld. Trial Court, while passing the impugned order under revision has ignored all such aspects of the case and framed the charges against the petitioner.
26. The respondent no. 3 / complainant has alleged in her complaint dated 08.10.2012 that her JETHANI Shashi used to treat her with mental cruelty.

She has also alleged that her JETHANI Shashi had admitted that she was having physical relation with the husband of the respondent no. 3 / complainant and this complainant was kept for social cause and on finding opportunity, she would be killed.

But, as the perusal of the record reveals that the marriage of the respondent no. 3 /
complainant with Sh. Laxminarayan (who has committed suicide and stated to be expired on dated 11.12.2018) was solemnized on dated 10.02.2003 and this respondent no. 3 / complainant lived with her husband till 23.05.2012 and filed the complaint dated 08.10.2012 and FIR on dated 08.11.2014.

The statement of the respondent no. 3 / complainant recorded on dated 13.09.2017 u/s. 164 of CrPC by the Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate reveals no categorical date or time are mentioned, when Ms.
Shashi had dealt with mental cruelty to this respondent no. 3/complainant.

This respondent no.3/complainant has also not mentioned in her complaint or in her statement as to on which date,
Ms. Shashi had admitted that she had physical relation with her husband Laxminarayan.

As, the perusal of the record reveals that this respondent no.3/complainant lived with her husband since 10.02.2003 till 23.05.2012 and the respondent no.3/complainant has no where mentioned in her complaint or statement, as to what kind of mental cruelty is caused by Ms. Shashi to her.
It is submitted by the counsel for the petitioner that Ms. Shashi is living out of Delhi.

It is not disputed either by the counsel for the respondent no. 3/complainant or the Ld. APP for the State and if Ms.
Shashi is residing out of Delhi, then it was incumbent on the part of the respondent no.
3/complainant to show as to on which date, time and place, Ms. Shashi had dealt with mental cruelty.

But, the respondent no. 3/complainant has levelled general allegation of dealing this respondent no. 3/complainant with mental cruelty that to without stating any date, time or place,
so, such bald assertion were not sufficient to frame charge against Ms. Shashi.
